title: LEBRE research record — v0.52-r1
description:
Research record of LEBRE (Lifecycle-governed Evidence-Based Resource Evolution), an online one-step-ahead forecaster for time series with inputs, designed for a budget of a few hundred floating-point operations per step. Each structural change (adding, removing, swapping or refining the response to a whole input) is accepted by an anytime-valid sequential test (e-process) of predictive improvement, within an online multiple-testing procedure.

This archive contains the complete record behind the LEBRE v0.52 specification, revision 1: the Python reference implementation, a C99 port, firmware and scripts for a simulated Cortex-M4F microcontroller (Renode), experiment scripts, pre-registrations, result tables, reports, frozen versions with SHA-256 manifests, the specification documents (English and Portuguese), and scripts to verify integrity and to reproduce results. Raw third-party data, per-series prediction arrays and toolchains are not included; they are listed with SHA-256 in ARTIFACTS_MANIFEST.tsv.

Scope and limits. The results cover hydrology (ONS, CAMELS-BR) and building energy (BDG2) series with 1–5 inputs and one-step forecasting. v0.52 is a frozen research version, not promoted. The e-values are valid under the stated assumptions, and false-change control was verified empirically. The declared cost contract was narrowly not met (+3.7% mean, +2.0% peak). Microcontroller costs come from a simulator, not a board. The testing mechanism did not improve accuracy over an all-inputs-on ablation. The core mechanism is not original. See the specification, section 19.
